transcript.content: Hi, welcome in. I'm Dr. Smith. To start, can you tell me what brings you in today?

Well… I’m here because people keep telling me I’m making too much of it, and I don’t want to sound unreasonable, Doctor. But I know what’s been going on. My wife’s relative came into our house to get at me. My tools don’t just move on their own, and my fishing plans don’t get messed up every weekend by accident.

It’s been months of this, and I can see pretty clearly he’s trying to take over my place and push me out. I just… I need someone to understand that I’m not imagining it.
Besides these experiences with your tools and plans, have you ever heard voices or sounds that others don't seem to hear, or seen things that others don't see?

No, I don’t think so. I mean, I haven’t been seeing things or hearing voices or anything like that. It’s more… things that happen, real things I notice. I’m not trying to sound strange. Does that make sense?
Do you have any medical conditions—like thyroid problems, seizures, or head injuries—or do you use alcohol or drugs, that started around the same time these beliefs began?

I don’t think so, Doctor. I mean… nothing like that comes to mind around when this all started. I don’t use drugs or anything. I’m not a heavy drinker. And I haven’t had, you know, some big head injury or seizures that I know of.

I hope that’s the kind of thing you mean. I just haven’t noticed anything medical that explains it.
Aside from these beliefs, have you noticed any changes in your ability to keep up with work, take care of daily tasks, or maintain relationships since this started?

No, not really… I mean, I’m still doing what I’m supposed to do. I get up, go to the plant, do my assembler work, keep the bills paid, shower, eat, all that. I don’t want you thinking I’m falling apart or anything.

The problem is really just what’s going on at the house—with him, and my things being messed with. That’s where the trouble is centered, if that makes sense.

final_diagnosis.reason: Patient presents with a fixed, non-bizarre persecutory delusion (belief that wife's relative is sabotaging his belongings and plans to force him out) persisting for several months. No hallucinations, no disorganized speech/behavior, and no negative symptoms are present. Mood symptoms are not reported. Functioning is preserved across occupational, self-care, and most social domains, with disturbance limited to the delusional theme. No medical, neurological, or substance-related etiology identified. This clinical picture—an isolated, non-bizarre delusion with preserved functioning and absence of other psychotic domains—is most consistent with Delusional Disorder (F22) rather than Schizophrenia (which requires broader symptom domains and functional decline) or Other Psychotic Disorder.
